headline: Secure Old Rag Tickets and Skyline Drive Entrance Information
reservation: Shenandoah National Park requires a standard entrance fee or pass. A separate, specific ticket is required for hiking Old Rag Mountain during the peak season to manage trail volume; these must be obtained via Recreation.gov. In-park lodging at Skyland or Big Meadows should be booked well in advance through the official concessionaire, especially for October foliage.

days.title: The High Ridges of Skyline Drive

stops.name: Rockfish Gap Entrance
stops.detail: Begin your journey at the southern end of the park and stop at the first few overlooks for valley views.

stops.name: Byrd Visitor Center
stops.detail: Explore the history of the park's creation and check current mountain weather forecasts at Big Meadows.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours including stops on the winding drive; conditions vary
days.note: Skyline Drive has a strictly enforced speed limit of 35 mph to protect wildlife and visitors.

days.title: Waterfalls and Central Summits

stops.name: Dark Hollow Falls
stops.detail: Hike down to the park’s most famous waterfall; remember the return trip is a steep uphill climb.

stops.name: Stony Man Trail
stops.detail: Follow the Appalachian Trail section to a rocky outcrop offering views of the Shenandoah Valley and Luray.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for transit between central trailheads; conditions vary
days.note: Parking lots for popular trails like Dark Hollow Falls often reach capacity by mid-morning.

days.title: Northern Peaks and Wilderness

stops.name: Hawksbill Summit
stops.detail: Reach the highest point in the park for a 360-degree view of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

stops.name: Limberlost Trail
stops.detail: Walk the accessible circuit through greenstone forests and mountain laurel thickets.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours to traverse toward the Thornton Gap exit; conditions vary
days.note: Fog can significantly reduce visibility and slow travel times on the ridge without warning.

intel.title: Skyline Drive Overlooks
intel.text: Use designated paved pull-outs for all sightseeing; stopping in the travel lane is prohibited and dangerous on curves. Trailhead lots are small and do not accommodate oversized vehicles or RVs effectively.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Effects
intel.text: Cell service is intermittent along Skyline Drive and typically fails in the hollows near waterfalls. A physical park map from the entrance station is essential for navigating trail junctions.

intel.title: In-Park Service Stations
intel.text: Fuel is only available at Big Meadows (Mile 51) and seasonally at other locations; confirm current hours before heading to the north or south ends. Gateway towns like Luray and Front Royal offer full services.

intel.title: Seasonal Foliage Peaks
intel.text: October brings heavy traffic and full parking lots; midweek visits are suggested to avoid the longest delays. Spring wildflower blooms vary by elevation, starting in the valleys and moving up the ridge.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: Skyline Drive may close due to snow, ice, or high winds at any time during the winter months. Check the official NPS automated road phone line or website before attempting a winter visit.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Charlottesville–Albemarle Airport (CHO); stock up on groceries in Charlottesville or Elkton before entering through Swift Run or Rockfish Gap.
plan.vehicle: Cars are ideal for the tight curves of Skyline Drive; RVs must check clearance for Marys Rock Tunnel (12'8") and verify campground length limits.
plan.goldenHour: Little Stony Man Overlook for sunset views over the Page Valley, depending on mountain haze.
